title: Ridgeline Pro Credit Ledger Rule — Return Credits and Credit Balance Refunds
content:
## Return credits

A refund for merchandise, an order, a service or a rental that was charged to a Ridgeline Pro Credit account is credited to the same account against the invoice that charged it, referencing that invoice and its invoice number. It is never paid out in cash and never moved to another account.

- **Amount.** The amount is the refund decided under the selling program's own rules, and the credits referencing one invoice may never total more than that invoice's amount.
- **Account status.** A return credit is accepted on accounts whose status is active, on hold, closed or charged off, as shown on the account record.
- **Effect.** A credit against an invoice that is still open reduces that invoice's open balance; a credit against an invoice already paid leaves a credit on account that the next payment application absorbs.

| Invoice state when the credit posts | Effect of the credit |
|---|---|
| Still open | Reduces that invoice's open balance |
| Already paid | Leaves a credit on account, absorbed by the next payment application |

Hypothetical example: an invoice of 900.00 has already received a return credit of 700.00. A further refund against it can be credited only up to 200.00, because the credits referencing one invoice may not total more than 900.00.

## Credit balance refunds

When the account carries a credit balance above the tier's credit balance refund threshold, an owner or principal may ask for it to be refunded in full as one credit balance refund. A credit balance at or below the threshold stays on the account.

The request is the caller's — an owner or principal of the business asks — and the size of the credit balance is the one the account record shows.

Hypothetical pair on a Pro Revolving Charge (threshold 1.00): a credit balance of 1.00 stays on the account; a credit balance of 64.20 may, at an owner's request, be refunded in full as one refund of 64.20.
